# Paragraph-mark editing controls

Original OOXML generated by `tools/paragraph_mark_edit_fixture.py`, using the
repository's original script-size control package as the supporting OPC shell.
No third-party document content or fonts are embedded.

Each case begins with `AB` (24 pt text, 12 pt blue paragraph mark) and `CD`
(30 pt text, 18 pt red paragraph mark). Offsets address `AB\nCD`.
`tools/record-paragraph-mark-edit.ps1` opens its own temporary copy in the reference application, processes cases backwards, and saves the native output separately.
`native-recording.json` records the native build, methods and SHA-256 hashes.
`records.json` records actual resulting paragraph counts/text, avoiding assumed
counts when the reference application's selection behavior differs. The COM Selection methods are
native object-model evidence, not a physical-keyboard or IME recording.

Ten cases establish that inserted marks take the typing format and the original
final mark remains attached to the retained suffix. Deleting just a paragraph
break retains the trailing mark. The model and DOCX round-trip tests compare
these cases in both selection directions, including undo and untouched parts.

The `merge-middle` case remains unresolved: The reference application's Selection.Delete(1,1) on
`B\rC` leaves `A\rD`, whereas our explicit range replacement leaves `AD`.
The native evidence is retained and hash/text checked, but this case is excluded
from the equivalence assertion. Do not treat that exclusion as conformance or
change the evidence to fit the model. Investigate selection/deletion semantics
separately before adopting the reference application's behavior.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.29 defines paragraph-mark rPr; the editor's assignment
of formats during input is application behavior, not a proven spec divergence.
